messages:
Sofia (support): hey team, customer rwd-telemetry reported repeated 429s and some 401/402s over a 20m window. They were hitting rwd3-medium with ~120 reqs/min sustained, occasional bursts to 400rpm. Request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. They say it started once they enabled long-context (32k).

Marcus (eng): can you paste the raw logs or a curl repro? curious if this is per-model throttle or an auth/billing fallback. 429s + 401/402 mixed makes me think of quota exhaustion -> auth fallback path.

Sofia (support): log snippets: 
```
[2026-03-14T15:02:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d model=rwd3-medium ctx_tokens=32768 status=429 reason=rate_limit_exceeded svc_code=RATE_PER_MIN
[2026-03-14T15:03:45Z] req=req_0a1b2c3e status=401 reason=auth_failure token_status=valid=false
[2026-03-14T15:05:09Z] req=req_0a1b2c3f status=402 reason=billing_blocked account_id=acct_9f8
```

Sofia (support): customer ran this curl to repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-medium","input":"<~32k tokens...>","stream":false}'
```

Priya (sre): early take: per-model RPM/TPM + concurrency limits are enforced at the router level. long context increases token accounting and sometimes causes internal queueing; if queued time exceeds internal threshold we can surface 429 to the client. Also, if the customer's billing account hit a threshold mid-run, subsequent requests return 402 and auth may reject (401) for rotated/invalid tokens.

Marcus (eng): confirmed. For rwd3-medium current enforced defaults (public doc reference): per-model RPM = 300 rpm, TPM = 1.2M tpm, max concurrency = 40 per org (varies by tier). When a request has huge context (>=16k) we apply a heavier token penalty that counts against TPM, so sustained 120 req/min at 32k tokens will push TPM quickly.

Marcus (eng): repro steps I ran locally (simulated):
```
# node script that sends concurrent requests with jitter
// pseudo
for (let i=0;i<6;i++) setTimeout(()=>fetch(...), i*200);
```
When I ramp to sustained 100rpm with 32k payloads I see throttles after ~10-15m and increasing 429s.

Sofia (support): customer also reported spikes aligned with nightly billing job at ~15:00 UTC. Could be their balance got depleted and billing webhook didn't finish before requests resumed.

QuotaBot: automated note: customer acct_9f8 hit soft TPM threshold at 2026-03-14T14:58:00Z. Current usage: 1,250,345 tokens in 60m window. Soft thresholds cause advisory warnings; hard thresholds cause 429/402 enforcement.

Priya (sre): action plan:
- confirm account billing status (billing team)
- check Dedicated/Dedicated-like route fallbacks (if they were routed to backup cluster with lower capacities)
- get full X-Request-Id traces for the 401s to see auth path failures
- reproduce with a controlled script and capture router traces

Marcus (eng): quick mitigations to offer customer:
- reduce context length where possible (chunk prompts, use embeddings + retrieval to shorten active context)
- apply client-side rate limiting + token-aware accounting. eg: treat each large-context request as N normal requests for backoff.
- add exponential backoff + jitter, and a fallback to a lower-capacity model variant (rwd3-small) with pinned compatibility.

Sofia (support): I replied to customer with: "We're seeing your account hit TPM soft limit due to sustained large-context requests. Recommended: reduce active context or stagger requests; we'll investigate billing webhook and router traces. If you need sustained throughput at 32k, consider Dedicated or request a quota increase." :thumbsup:

BillingBot: acct_9f8 invoice status: past_due -> triggered temporary billing block at 2026-03-14T15:00:10Z. This explains the 402s. Customer has a resumed payment attempt at 2026-03-14T15:06:00Z which cleared the block.

Marcus (eng): interesting — that sequence (TPM high -> billing block -> 402 -> token refresh attempts -> 401) yields the mixed errors. We should add an internal note to correlate token refresh failures with billing events.

Priya (sre): added steps to reproduce in staging and will capture router + kv-cache metrics. Also toggling context_penalty config in staging to see how quickly TPM accumulates.

Sofia (support): final notes to include in case file for support playbook:
- look up per-model RPM/TPM in Console -> Models -> Limits (org-level overrides possible)
- watch for long-context token multipliers (>=16k and >=32k tiers)
- check account billing events for 402s and token rotation attempts for 401s
- advise client-side token-aware rate limiting, jittered retries, and fallback model variants
- escalate to Dedicated sales if sustained high-TPM with long context required

Marcus (eng): assigning follow-ups: @Priya to collect traces and @Sofia to confirm billing resolution with customer and close once they confirm stability.

Sofia (support): noted. I'll follow up in 2hrs with customer status. :hourglass:
